reviews.title: Just the best - EDITED from 5stars to 1
reviews.text:
I'm not a business, or a student so probably haven't investigated all this marvellous little app can do.   But I do do a lot of study and like to highlight, underline and add notes to the books and magazines I have stored within it.   For my purposes it is ideal.   Quick and simple to use.   Would really like to delete the photo folder it's installed, and appears I can't so that's a mild irritant, but that's my only gripe.  Stores and plays my music files too! Loved it before and love it now!

EDIT After many years of happy use, I’m now transferring my files elsewhere and actively looking for an alternative.  There is so much now stuck behind a paywall that Documents is not the tool it was.  A one of payment would have been fine or a more reasonable subscription, but I’m not in a position to pay what Readdle are now asking.   My student children can’t afford it either so they’ve deleted and moved on too.  Shame!

reviews.title: Not what I expected
reviews.text:
Seems like a cool app but missing the entire definition of FILE MANAGER.
Downloaded this at the recommendation of Gemini to get around Apples stupid inability to move more than a handful of files at a time (said this was the solution).

Looked great at first because it allowed me to select a bunch of files, but just copied them into its own directory taking up double the space… and wouldn’t let me move them to SSD or anywhere else, only copy.
Also wouldn’t allow me to batch select files, after the initial load screen.

So tried the free trial and exact same results.
So garbage for what I need.

reviews.title: Quite poor
reviews.text:
It's really quite poor. It's supposed to be able to manage files on your device and in the cloud, but with any cloud interaction it's always running three operations from an invisible queue, and it reprioritises what it's doing seemingly at random. Nothing is ever finished until everything is finished - which either doesn't happen or happens way in the future. There's no way to see the queue, let alone manage it. There's no way to tell it to just do one thing at a time. It's plain bad. I don't know who's writing the 5 star reviews.

They update it all the time, and with every update there's a tour of how they changed some trivial thing that you'd never notice. Almost every time I open it there's a new tour, and company news - as if anyone is interested. It's a horrible user experience that seems to stem from narcissism on the marketing side. The company doesn't seem to realise it's a utility app, not a fashion brand.

And as if that's not bad enough, it routinely sends pop-ups to tell you some files haven't been opened (if they haven't been). Because we must all open everything with Documents. How it does this when it's closed I don't know. Is it sending detailed usage info for every file, along with the file names up to Readdle?

Truly this company's apps have fallen from grace recently. I'm guessing either the staff have nothing to do, so change for change sake, or they have a poorly suited new leader that's wrecking everything.

reviews.title: Top-Notch app, massively overpriced
reviews.text:
A best-in-class app for many years, now crippled with limited functionality because of developers’ greed.  Without warning or mention of change, Readdle sneakily removed functionality in a recent update making previously inclusive features expensive subscription-only.

They described the update as improving the experience by resolving issues and enhancing performance. This maybe, but they neglected to mention the removal of functionality. This is underhanded behaviour. Yes, charge a subscription for NEW features and let people decide if they want them or not; don’t remove features which always worked. 

They say certain “advanced tools” which are part of Documents Plus subscription were temporarily accessible due to a technical issue and these features were not intended to be available without a Documents Plus subscription. 

I’ve been using Documents for over a decade, so these features were certainly not temporary, they have always been available.  When they introduced the Documents plus subscription it did provide more features, but these were unnecessary for my needs as an older person on minimum fixed income, I don’t want AI features. 

I know app developers need to make money, this doesn’t mean they should rip people off.  I’d pay a single one-off £20 payment (or even £1.99 a year) to unlock features, but certainly not 9.99 a month!  This is way too expensive.  It’s not only Readdle who are guilty of overcharging; This subscription madness needs to stop.
